_comment: A pack plan for tools/generate.py and gen.cmd. Either a bare array of jobs or {"jobs": [...], "project": "..."}. Run it with:  gen.cmd -p games/new_local_game -j assets\pack.example.json

_field_notes.kind: image = prompt -> PNG | mask = image -> alpha PNG | 3d = image -> GLB ('character' is an alias of 3d) | upscale = image -> bigger PNG (Real-ESRGAN) | recolor = image + prompt -> PNG (z-image img2img, global restyle) | edit = 1-2 images + instruction -> PNG (Qwen-Image-Edit, keeps the composition and can write lettering)
_field_notes.from: name of an EARLIER job in this same list - keeps the whole pack inside one ComfyUI session
_field_notes.image: alternative to `from`: a path to an existing image, relative to the project
_field_notes.images: kind=edit only: the LIST spelling of the above, in graph order - the first entry is <image1> in the instruction and it is also what sets the output's aspect ratio. To change the shape, change the reference; there is no size knob.
_field_notes.out: target path relative to the project. Omit the extension to get the natural one. Without `out` it goes to public/assets/<images|masks|3d>/<name>.<ext>
_field_notes.quality: 3d only: economy = TripoSplat ~3 min (unlit, no UVs) | high = Pixal3D/TRELLIS.2 ~18 min (UV + PBR, for a lit scene)
_field_notes.megapixels: the ACTUAL size of the picture: 1.0 ~= 1024x1024, 0.25 ~= 512x512. Cost scales with area, so 0.25 is roughly four times cheaper than the default - use it for textures.
_field_notes.strength: recolor only: how far img2img may drift (0.1-0.95). There is no setting that both keeps the composition and changes the palette; use edit for that.

jobs.name: nova-concept
jobs.prompt: a small blue fox with a glowing cyan tail, full body, side view, plain pale background, stylised game art

jobs.name: grass-tuft
jobs.prompt: a single tuft of stylised grass, flat shading, plain background, game texture

jobs.prompt: a small mossy stone shrine with a glowing blue crystal, stylised game asset

jobs.name: nova-keyart
jobs.prompt: Replace the figure standing on the rock in <image1> with the fox from <image2>, same pose and same scale. Keep the background, the lighting, the palette and the title text exactly as they are in <image1>.
